cells.tense: You are tending something living right now, and you are holding it well.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Something you've been tending has reached its own fullness. Let it stand untouched and keep your hands for what is still growing.
cells.core:
You learn how things grow by tending them. On this stretch something living is in your hands and you are holding it well — steady, patient, not forcing the pace. You don't need to know how it turns out; you're in the middle of it, and that's where you do your best work.

What this calls for now is knowing when to stop. A crop is already ripe. Let it stand, not out of neglect but because its season is complete. The care you meant for it moves to the next row. Your strength for carrying weight isn't lessened by that — it's refined.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing, and you can tell when it's done.
cells.verb: Learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: On the long stretch where you're the one holding it up

cells.tense: Every branch of what you're building is being lived three seasons ahead of where it's growing.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Where your life runs ahead of itself, trade certainty for curiosity. Wonder at something that hasn't happened yet, and decide nothing about it.
cells.core:
Tending something living is your way, and when the season is right you hold steady through the slow parts. You water what's there, you don't force the growth, and the thing comes up in its own time. Lately that patience has tipped. What's ahead is being lived as if it were already here — branches planned, outcomes rehearsed, possibilities held before they've had a chance to become. What you carry is being carried three seasons past where it's growing.

Let the unknown back in. One unborn thing gets your curiosity instead of your surety — not a plan for it, just wonder at what it might become. The vision you're forcing can wait until the roots have something to say.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing a future the roots haven't reached yet.
cells.verb: Learning how things grow by tending them

cells.tense: The door you're still standing in front of was closed some seasons ago.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something today that interests you and has no plan attached — no outcome, no purpose beyond the beginning itself.
cells.core:
The part of you that tends living things has gone quiet. What you once cared for has been left behind — not by failure, but by time. The ground you're standing on is familiar, and the door ahead of you has already closed. You've been very still in front of it.

New life doesn't come back by deciding to care again. It comes by starting something alive — a seed you don't need to understand, a direction with no destination. You don't have to feel ready first. The spark doesn't shine because you willed it; it shines when what you've started grows into its own light.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you, and you're still waiting there.
cells.verb: Learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: On the long stretch where you're the one holding it up

cells.tense: The center of what you're carrying is you, and you've been keeping that out of the room.
cells.act: bear the duty and know when to let go
cells.ask: Name what you bear that finished long ago but you've kept shouldering. Set that part down, and keep the rest for now.
cells.core:
Something is being carried that doesn't have anyone visible carrying it. You've done the long haul of it — watching it grow, keeping it steady — and your version of the story has you just going about your business. That story makes the work look like terrain rather than a hand under it.

The beginning of it was simpler: a seed you planted because you wanted to see it grow. That's the part worth finding again. Take up one small act of care that nobody asked for and that has no hurry in it. Not to fill the role, but because somewhere under the long haul of it, you were someone who liked to watch things come up.
